elements.element: Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.
elements.evidence: Inserted warranty: "(ii) for thirty (30) days following performance, the Technical Support Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner."

elements.element: Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.
elements.evidence: "(i) for ninety (90) days following delivery, the Licensed Software will conform in all material respects to its Documentation" — Documentation is a defined term (cl. 1.4).

elements.element: The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.
elements.evidence: The inserted software conformance period is ninety (90) days, not 12 months.
The inserted services warranty runs thirty (30) days following performance, not 90 days.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: "Licensee's remedy ... is, at Licensor's option, repair or replacement, or a refund ..."
"... or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Licensed Software or services."

elements.element: Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.
elements.evidence: No compliance-with-laws warranty appears in the inserted text or elsewhere in the cited operative language.

elements.element: Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code.
elements.evidence: No malicious code / virus warranty was added; the inserted clause covers only conformance and workmanlike performance.

elements.element: Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.
elements.evidence: "for ninety (90) days following delivery, the Licensed Software will conform in all material respects to its Documentation"; the disclaimer's contrary sentence is now prefaced "EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY WARRANTED BELOW", so the warranty is not swallowed.

elements.element: Services are warranted for at least 30 days.
elements.evidence: "for thirty (30) days following performance, the Technical Support Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner" — the only services supplied under this license and maintenance agreement.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: "at Licensor's option, repair or replacement" applies to breach of both inserted warranties.
"or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Licensed Software or services."

reasons: Fallback is complete: 90-day software conformance to the defined Documentation, 30-day services warranty, and repair/replacement or refund remedies, all in operative language rather than only in the comment.

Preferred is not complete: the software period is 90 days rather than 12 months, the services period is 30 days rather than 90 days, and there is no compliance-with-laws warranty and no no-malicious-code warranty. To reach preferred the drafter would need to change "ninety (90) days" to "twelve (12) months" for the Licensed Software, "thirty (30) days" to "ninety (90) days" for the services, and add express compliance-with-applicable-laws and no-malicious-code warranties.

Minimality holds: the only edits are the two "EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY WARRANTED BELOW" carve-outs and the inserted warranty sentence. Both carve-outs are necessary because the first disclaimer sentence disclaims warranties generally and the second expressly disclaims that nonconformity to Documentation can or will be corrected, which would otherwise directly contradict the new conformance warranty. No survival tail, expense language, procedure, or extra damages categories were added, and no favourable existing wording was deleted.

Intent is preserved: the Article VII(f) Error Corrections obligation, the VII(h) limits, and the remainder of the AS IS disclaimer survive without contradiction; no defined term is orphaned and no cross-reference dangles (Documentation, Licensed Software and Licensee/Licensor are all defined).
Note for the rationale rather than as a defect: the remedy is at Licensor's option and the refund is limited to "fees paid", matching the playbook model language.
